correctness.rationale: Canonical unordered rooted-forest representation of (P4,C4)-free trivially perfect graphs is exhaustive and nonduplicating by recursive deletion of universal vertices. Independent reimplementation enumerated exactly 1,2,4,9,20,48,115,286,719 graphs for orders 1..9 and two color-refinement recurrences agreed. Three strict rounds first occur at n=8 with unique star+paw disjoint union; connected first at n=9 unique cone. This is a complete finite classification, not extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The natural minimal-order complete classification for three strict 1-WL splits in trivially perfect graphs and its connected subclass is not implied by general unrestricted iteration extremality or foundational color refinement definitions. Its originality is a specific exhaustive graph-family fact, with no claim of a general asymptotic classification.
residual_risks: A specialized unindexed computation of small trivially-perfect graph refinement depths could duplicate these finite thresholds.
The theorem only classifies the earliest three strict refinements; no inference for large-order maximal depth or amenability follows.
